subject: BrightEdge Health — inference fit & playbook (post-call summary)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Sanchez <olivia.sanchez@brightedge.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: BrightEdge Health — inference fit & playbook (post-call summary)

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side + proposed playbook so we stay aligned. I pulled this together from Ben / Marissa's notes.

Top-level goals you shared:
- Reduce clinician response time on triage workflows (target: 40% faster average response)
- Move to on-prem inference for PHI-sensitive flows, but evaluate hybrid routing for non-PHI requests
- Keep per-token costs under $0.0006 for high-volume triage endpoints

Key pain points mentioned:
- Current latency spikes at peak hours; batch + KV cache behavior is unpredictable
- Security evidence needed (SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration) to satisfy procurement
- In-house model ops team needs a clear runbook for canary rollouts and fallback behavior

Proposed Redwood playbook (high level):
1) Pilot (4 weeks): Dedicated private deployment in your Azure VNet -> run triage model behind our private control plane; enable KV prefix caching and short-burst autoscaling.
2) Instrumentation + metrics (week 1–2): Per-route latency and token-cost dashboards; add synthetic probes for 99th percentile SLO validation.
3) Integration changes we recommend: small SDK change to adopt streaming function-calls for incremental replies; structured JSON output (schema v1) for EHR ingestion; embeddings for rerank on historical notes.
4) Security & procurement: provide SOC2 artifact bundle + KMS integration doc, and surface audit logs for last 90 days.

Open technical asks for BrightEdge team (action items):
- Provide sample 1,000-message workload and max sequence length distribution (due: 10/18)
- Confirm list of endpoints that will be PHI vs non-PHI (due: 10/18)
- Confirm preferred KMS vendor and whether a HSM-backed key is required (due: 10/20)

Attachments: BrightEdge_Mutual_Action_Plan_20261011.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones), BrightEdge_Security_QA_asks.pdf (initial security artifacts checklist).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share the MAP and a short SOW draft by EOD Monday (10/12).
- Ben / Marissa will follow up with a technical clarification email and a short checklist for SDK/streaming changes.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week for model sizing + latency SLOs (target: 10/19).

If that matches your read, reply with any edits and we'll lock things in.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0183

From: Olivia Sanchez <olivia.sanchez@brightedge.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: BrightEdge Health — inference fit & playbook (post-call summary)

Priya — thanks for the concise summary, this is very helpful. High-level confirmation from our side:

- Goals and pain points: confirmed. Latency at peak is our #1 operational headache; cost target makes sense.
- Hybrid is the right path: we'd like critical PHI flows to stay on-prem, but we want to evaluate hybrid routing for anonymized queries.
- Workload sample: we'll export a 1,000-message sample and the endpoint mapping by 10/18.
- KMS: we currently use Azure Key Vault, but procurement will confirm HSM need by 10/20.

A couple clarifications / asks:
1) Can your pilot run inside our subscription (we prefer that) or does Redwood need to provision in your environment?
2) For the structured JSON output, can you send the schema draft ahead of the technical call so our EHR team can review?

I'll loop Aidan from AWS Marketplace if we pursue a marketplace procurement path — he can confirm listing requirements on their side.

Appreciate the action items. We'll reply with the workload export early next week.

Best,
Olivia Sanchez
VP, Product Operations | BrightEdge Health
olivia.sanchez@brightedge.com | +1 (206) 555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: BrightEdge Health — inference fit & playbook (post-call summary)

Internal notes / technical follow-ups for the deep-dive:

1) SDK changes: recommend adding a small optional streaming callback that emits partial function-call arguments. Minimal surface: one additional callback parameter and a backwards-compatible flag (enable_partial_funcalls: true). That keeps the client changes lightweight.

2) Structured output: propose schema v0.1 fields: {"triage_label": string, "confidence": float, "extracted_entities": [{"type": string, "text": string}], "metadata": {}} — I'll put this in a short doc and share before the deep-dive.

3) Performance: target deployment on 8xA10G in the private VNet for the pilot; enable KV cache warmers and a 200ms p50 target for short sequences. We'll include autoscaling rules to cap token-per-second to meet cost guardrails.

4) Security artifacts: I'll assemble the SOC2 artifact bundle and a short KMS integration guide (Azure Key Vault steps + sample Terraform snippet).

Action for Marissa: can you pull a quick template runbook for canary + automatic fallback policy (we prefer model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model) and drop into the MAP?

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
